stem: Which taxpayer qualifies for head of household status for 2025?

choices.text: A widow whose spouse died in 2025
A married taxpayer living with her spouse all year
choices.explanation: Married taxpayers living together can't use HOH.

choices.text: An unmarried parent who pays all costs of a home where her dependent son lived all year
choices.explanation: Correct. HOH: unmarried, maintains a home for a qualifying person for more than half the year.

explanation: HOH: unmarried, maintains a home for a qualifying person for more than half the year.

stem: Which person can be a qualifying relative (not a qualifying child) for 2025?

choices.text: The taxpayer's 15-year-old daughter who lived with him all year
A friend who lived with the taxpayer for 6 months
choices.explanation: Household members must live there all year.

choices.text: The taxpayer's widowed father with $4,000 of taxable interest income whom the taxpayer supports
choices.explanation: Correct. Qualifying relative: relationship, gross income under $5,200, over half support.

choices.text: The taxpayer's brother with $12,000 of wages

explanation: Qualifying relative: relationship, gross income under $5,200, over half support.

stem: What is the 2025 basic standard deduction for a married couple filing jointly (under 65, not blind)?

choices.explanation: Correct. The One Big Beautiful Bill Act set the 2025 MFJ standard deduction at $31,500.

explanation: The One Big Beautiful Bill Act set the 2025 MFJ standard deduction at $31,500.
reviewNote: Uses a One Big Beautiful Bill Act (P.L. 119-21) amount for 2025. Verify against current IRS guidance and exam materials.

stem: Which item is taxable to the recipient?

choices.text: $50,000 of life insurance proceeds paid on the insured's death
A $5,000 cash award for winning an essay contest
choices.explanation: Correct. Prizes and awards are generally included.

choices.text: Compensatory damages for a physical injury

explanation: Prizes and awards are generally included.

stem: An employee receives employer-paid group-term life insurance coverage of $50,000 and a $300 holiday gift card. What is included in gross income?

choices.text: The cost of the coverage only
choices.explanation: The coverage is excluded; the card isn't.

choices.text: The cost of $50,000 of coverage plus $300
choices.explanation: The first $50,000 of coverage is excluded.
Correct. §79 excludes $50,000 of coverage; cash equivalents are never de minimis.

explanation: §79 excludes $50,000 of coverage; cash equivalents are never de minimis.

stem: A cash-basis taxpayer is insolvent by $15,000 when a lender cancels $40,000 of debt (not in bankruptcy). What is included in income?

choices.explanation: Correct. Excluded to the extent of insolvency: 40,000 − 15,000 = 25,000 included.

explanation: Excluded to the extent of insolvency: 40,000 − 15,000 = 25,000 included.

stem: A taxpayer receives $6,000 of unemployment compensation and $8,000 of child support. How much is included in gross income?

choices.explanation: Includes child support and excludes unemployment — reversed.
Correct. Unemployment compensation is taxable; child support isn't.

explanation: Unemployment compensation is taxable; child support isn't.

stem: A taxpayer rents a vacation home for 120 days and uses it personally for 20 days. How is it classified?

choices.text: A rental property with full deductions
choices.explanation: Personal use exceeds 14 days (greater of 14 or 10% of 120 = 14).

choices.text: A residence; rental deductions are limited to rental income
choices.explanation: Correct. Personal use of 20 days exceeds the greater of 14 days or 12 days (10% of 120).

explanation: Personal use of 20 days exceeds the greater of 14 days or 12 days (10% of 120).

stem: A single taxpayer with MAGI of $130,000 actively participates in a rental with a $20,000 loss and has no passive income. How much is deductible?

choices.explanation: The allowance isn't fully phased out.

stem: A sole proprietor incurs $400 for business meals with clients and $900 for golf outings with clients. What is deductible?

choices.explanation: Entertainment isn't deductible and meals are 50%.

explanation: Meals 50% (200); entertainment 0.

stem: Which is a deduction for AGI in 2025?

choices.text: Contributions to a health savings account
choices.explanation: Correct. HSA contributions made by the individual are above-the-line.

explanation: HSA contributions made by the individual are above-the-line.

stem: A single taxpayer (MAGI $70,000) is covered by a 401(k) and contributes $7,000 to a traditional IRA in 2025. How much is deductible?

choices.explanation: Correct. MAGI is below the $79,000 phase-out start.
MAGI is below the phase-out range.
That was an older contribution limit.

explanation: Active participants phase out at $79,000–$89,000 (single) for 2025.

stem: A taxpayer with AGI of $60,000 gives $40,000 cash to a public charity. What is the current-year deduction?

choices.explanation: Correct. Cash to public charities: 60% × 60,000 = 36,000; 5-year carryforward.

explanation: Cash to public charities: 60% × 60,000 = 36,000; 5-year carryforward.

stem: Which is deductible as an itemized deduction for 2025?

choices.text: Real estate taxes on a principal residence (within the SALT cap)
choices.explanation: Correct. Real property taxes are deductible subject to the SALT limit.

choices.text: Tax preparation fees for a personal return
Foreign real property taxes on a personal vacation home

explanation: Real property taxes are deductible subject to the SALT limit.

stem: A single taxpayer has QBI of $100,000 from a non-service business and taxable income before QBI of $90,000 (no capital gains). The taxpayer is below the threshold. What is the QBI deduction?

choices.explanation: Adds the components instead of taking the lesser.

stem: A married couple filing jointly (MAGI $180,000) has three children aged 5, 11, and 16. What is their 2025 child tax credit?
explanation: 2025 CTC is $2,200 per qualifying child under 17; the joint phase-out starts at $400,000.
reviewNote: Uses a One Big Beautiful Bill Act (P.L. 119-21) amount for 2025. Verify against current IRS guidance and exam materials.

stem: A student's parents (MAGI $150,000, joint) pay $3,000 of qualified tuition for her first year of college. What is the American opportunity credit?
explanation: AOTC = 100% of the first $2,000 + 25% of the next $1,000.

stem: Which credit can produce a refund even if the taxpayer owes no tax?
explanation: The EIC is refundable.

stem: A self-employed individual has $100,000 of net SE income and no wages. What is the deduction for half of SE tax (rounded)?

choices.explanation: Uses only the Social Security rate.

stem: Which item is a tax preference or adjustment for individual AMT?

choices.explanation: Correct. Private activity bond interest is an AMT preference.
Acquisition interest is allowed for AMT.
Allowed at the same floor for AMT.

explanation: Private activity bond interest is an AMT preference.

stem: A C corporation owns 85% of a domestic subsidiary and receives $200,000 of dividends. What is the dividends-received deduction?
explanation: 80% or more ownership → 100% DRD.

stem: A corporation's taxable income before charitable contributions, DRD, and NOL is $500,000. It contributed $70,000 cash to charity. What is the charitable deduction?
Which item is added to book income in reconciling to taxable income?

choices.text: Excess of tax depreciation over book depreciation

choices.explanation: Correct. Federal income tax isn't deductible, so it's added back.

explanation: Federal income tax isn't deductible, so it's added back.

stem: A corporation has 2025 taxable income of $200,000 before a $300,000 NOL carryforward from 2020. What is 2025 taxable income?

choices.explanation: The NOL can't create a loss.

explanation: Post-2017 NOL deduction limited to 80% of TI.

stem: When is the final estimated tax installment due for a calendar-year corporation?

choices.explanation: Correct. Corporate installments: 15th day of the 4th, 6th, 9th, and 12th months.

explanation: Corporate installments: 15th day of the 4th, 6th, 9th, and 12th months.

stem: A corporation has accumulated E&P of $10,000 and current E&P of $25,000. It distributes $50,000 to its sole shareholder (basis $40,000). What is the dividend?

choices.explanation: Correct. Dividend = 25,000 current + 10,000 accumulated = 35,000; 15,000 reduces basis.

explanation: Dividend = 25,000 current + 10,000 accumulated = 35,000; 15,000 reduces basis.

stem: A corporation distributes land (FMV $60,000; basis $20,000) to a shareholder. What gain does the corporation recognize?

choices.explanation: Gain is recognized on appreciated property.
That's the property's basis, not the gain.
Correct. §311(b): recognize gain as if sold.

explanation: §311(b): recognize gain as if sold.

stem: Which is most likely treated as a constructive dividend?

choices.text: Reasonable salary paid to a shareholder-employee
A corporation's payment of a shareholder's personal vacation
choices.explanation: Correct. Payments of shareholders' personal expenses are constructive dividends.

choices.text: Repayment of a bona fide loan from a shareholder
Rent paid to a shareholder at fair market rates

explanation: Payments of shareholders' personal expenses are constructive dividends.

stem: In a §351 exchange, a shareholder transfers property (basis $60,000; FMV $100,000) for stock worth $90,000 and $10,000 cash. What is her stock basis?
A shareholder owns 30% of a corporation; after a redemption she owns 20%. No attribution applies. Is the redemption substantially disproportionate?

choices.text: Yes — she owns less than 50% and less than 80% of 30% (24%)

choices.explanation: Complete termination isn't required for this test.

choices.text: No — she must own less than 10%

stem: A parent corporation owning 100% of a subsidiary receives the subsidiary's assets in a complete liquidation. What is the parent's basis in those assets?

choices.explanation: Correct. §332/§334(b): no gain or loss; carryover basis.
The parent takes the subsidiary's basis.

explanation: §332/§334(b): no gain or loss; carryover basis.

stem: A 50% partner's share of ordinary income is $40,000 and of tax-exempt interest $2,000; she receives $25,000 cash. Beginning basis is $10,000. What is her ending basis?
explanation: Income items increase basis; distributions decrease it.

stem: Which partnership item is **not** separately stated?

choices.text: Rent expense for the partnership's office
choices.explanation: Correct. It nets into ordinary business income.

explanation: Ordinary operating expenses net into ordinary business income.

stem: A partner with a $15,000 basis receives a current distribution of $5,000 cash and inventory with a partnership basis of $12,000. What is her basis in the inventory?

choices.explanation: Outside basis remains after the cash distribution.

explanation: Cash first reduces basis to 10,000; inventory takes the lesser of 12,000 or 10,000.

stem: A partnership pays a partner a $20,000 guaranteed payment for services. How does the partner treat it?

choices.text: As ordinary income subject to self-employment tax
choices.explanation: Correct. Guaranteed payments are ordinary income and SE income.

explanation: Guaranteed payments are ordinary income and SE income.

stem: Which requirement must be met to elect S corporation status?

choices.explanation: Correct. S corporations may have only one class of stock (voting differences allowed).

explanation: S corporations may have only one class of stock (voting differences allowed).

stem: An S corporation shareholder has stock basis of $5,000 and no debt basis. Her share of the corporation's loss is $12,000. How much is deductible?

choices.explanation: Correct. Losses limited to stock + debt basis; 7,000 is suspended.

explanation: Losses limited to stock + debt basis; 7,000 is suspended.

stem: A former C corporation (S since 2022) has accumulated E&P. Which distribution source comes first?

choices.explanation: Correct. Ordering: AAA → E&P → basis → gain.

explanation: Ordering: AAA → E&P → basis → gain.

stem: A donor gives $30,000 to a friend in 2025 and pays $12,000 directly to a hospital for the friend's surgery. What is the taxable gift?

choices.explanation: Medical payments made directly are excluded.
The cash gift exceeds the exclusion.

explanation: Direct medical payments are excluded; the cash gift exceeds the $19,000 exclusion by $11,000.

stem: Which income of a 501(c)(3) organization is most likely UBTI?

choices.text: Income from a regularly operated commercial parking garage open to the public, staffed by employees
choices.explanation: Correct. A regularly carried-on, unrelated trade or business produces UBTI.

choices.text: Proceeds of an annual volunteer-run bake sale

explanation: A regularly carried-on, unrelated trade or business produces UBTI.
